I stopped short of packaging the tarball, so let me hand you what I have plus the diagnosis, because the diagnosis is the important part and you can act on it immediately.

Your build isn't broken by a test — it's broken by 21 corrupted files
dotnet clean, restore, build, test, and the Containerfile build are all failing with the same error:

error MSB4024: The imported project file "Directory.Build.props" could not be loaded.
Data at the root level is invalid. Line 86, position 1.
Line 86 of Directory.Build.props is a line of eighty # characters appended after </Project>. MSBuild imports that file before it evaluates anything, so one malformed XML file fails every command you ran.

It is not the only file. I verified this byte-exactly against the Size: field in each METADATA block of dump.txt, and 21 tracked files carry the identical 82-byte suffix (\n + 80×# + \n):

.env.example · .github/workflows/ci.yml · .github/workflows/release.yml · Containerfile · Directory.Build.props · README.md · _CHANGES.md · docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md · docs/DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md · docs/OPERATIONS.md · docs/REQUIREMENTS.md · docs/TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md · Components/Layout/DisplayLayout.razor · Components/Layout/MainLayout.razor · Components/Pages/Home.razor · Configuration/RestaurantOptions.cs · Identity/ObligationsEnforcement.cs · Program.cs · wwwroot/app.css · tests/…/Identity/ObligationsEnforcementTests.cs · tests/…/RestaurantOptionsTests.cs

That set is exactly the modified files from the M6 close-out slice. The five new files from that slice are clean. That tells you the cause precisely: last session's packaging read modified files out of a split of dump.txt and kept the separator that export.sh writes between files. The authoritative end of a file in that format is the byte count in its METADATA block, not the separator that follows it.

And there is a second one you would never have found by looking at the ends of files: docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md has a buried separator at line 5760, between the Slice 16 section and the close-out section — the same damage from an earlier cycle, which the close-out then appended text after.

Once the separators are gone, everything parses: all 10 MSBuild/solution XML files, all 4 YAML files. The separator was the only damage. No truncation, no CRLF, no missing final newlines anywhere in the 309 files.

Why so much of it was silent
Of the 21 files, only 6 break anything: the one XML file (which breaks everything) and 5 C# files (CS1024, on a compile that never got to run). The other 15 absorbed it — it's a comment in YAML/Containerfile/.env, a heading rule in Markdown, literal page text in Razor markup, and a dangling selector in CSS that discards the rule after it. Your ci.yml and release.yml still parse perfectly while carrying the damage.

What I built before running out of tool calls
scripts/check_tree.sh — new blocking gate: no context-dump separators (export.sh exempt, threshold 20 not 80), no whitespace-only lines, LF + final newline, MSBuild XML parses (stdlib xml.etree), YAML parses (advisory when no parser, like your shellcheck gate). Clean under bash -n and shellcheck at both --severity=warning and --severity=style. I re-introduced the exact damage into a scratch copy and it caught all six problems, naming Directory.Build.props:86 and BUILD_PROGRESS.md:5761 by line.
scripts/ci_local.sh — tree hygiene inserted as gate 1, sections renumbered, help text updated. Re-linted clean.
Two genuine .editorconfig violations fixed so the whitespace gate lands at zero noise: compose.yaml:109 and DapperUserStorePasskeyTests.cs:228 (blank lines with leftover indentation).
Still to do: the tree job in ci.yml, the doc edits (§16.4, F-40, OPERATIONS §14, README, BUILD_PROGRESS), and the tarball itself.

If you want to unblock the build in the next thirty seconds without waiting for me, this reads the tree and touches nothing but those 21 files:

bash
cd /home/kushal/src/dotnet/myrestaurant
git ls-files | while IFS= read -r f; do grep -Iq -E '^#{20,}$' -- "$f" || continue
  [ "$f" = export.sh ] && continue; printf '%s\n' "$f"; done
Say continue and I'll ship the full tarball — all 21 restored files, the new gate, the ci.yml job, and the documentation, as complete files at their exact paths with a "Files to DELETE" section (which will be empty).
